plc.intro: {gates} stop gate(s) take their open and close commands from a PLC. A PLC reads the photo-eyes and the counters and writes the gates' coils; the model runs at the pace of the clock. The plant is kinematic: a PLC cannot make a belt faster.
plc.nogate: Set a stop gate's mode to "Set by a PLC" to give a PLC control of it. The photo-eyes are readable already.

shifts.note: A week that repeats; time 0 of a run is Monday 00:00. A station or source with a calendar starts no new work while it is off (work in progress finishes).

pools.title: Operator pools
pools.note: A group of people shared by stations. A station that names a pool needs one person from it for every load it serves; when nobody is free the load waits.

robot.note: Kinematics only: no collision checking, payload or dynamics. Times use each joint's speed and acceleration limits; they are a planning estimate, not a vendor controller's number. The program is a neutral text format; no robot maker's language is written.
robotx.table.dh: One row per joint, classic Denavit-Hartenberg: link length a, twist alpha, offset d, angle offset, then the joint limits and speed limits. Changes apply at once and are saved with the document.
robotx.table.scara: Two arm lengths, the slide's height range and the two arm angle ranges.
robotx.table.delta: Base and platform sizes, arm and rod lengths (Clavel) and the working height range (negative: below the base).
robotx.table.cartesian: The travel range of each slide in the robot's own frame.

robotx.fmt.hint: Choose which files to save for this cell. The path list is always saved. Your choice is kept with the document and remembered as your default.
robotx.fmt.unsupported: This format cannot describe a {type} robot.
robotx.fmt.unverified: Robot-language programs are minimal and unverified: generated from the model above, never run on a robot by CadCraft. Simulate and verify on your robot controller before running. Not endorsed by any robot maker.

robotx.refused.robot-type: This format cannot express a {type} robot.

robotx.omit.blend: blending (every move stops at its point)
robotx.omit.program: the program (this file is the robot only)
robotx.issue.io-syntax: Line {line}: write out N on or off, or waitin N on or off (N is 1 to 99).
plcmode.title: PLC mode
plcmode.safety.title: Simulation only.
plcmode.safety: Never drive real machinery from this emulation unattended, and never rely on it for safety: an emergency stop here is a test input. You are responsible for what a connected PLC does.
plcmode.noengine: The soft PLC engine (Digital twin files) could not be loaded in this build, so the PLC mode cannot run here.
plcmode.tags: {inputs} tags go from the model to the PLC (photo-eyes, gates read-back, counters); {outputs} come back (the gates' open commands).
plcmode.nogate: No stop gate is in PLC mode yet. Set a gate's mode to "Set by a PLC" so a controller can drive it.
plcmode.soft.intro: A soft PLC runs your program on the model, in this window or in Studio, with no hardware. Write Structured Text (IEC 61131-3) or paste PLCopen XML. Without a program the starter program is used.
plcmode.soft.run.hint: Repeatable: the same program and seed give the same result, faster than real time
plcmode.soft.attach.hint: Start Live in Run first; the soft PLC then scans with the model's clock
plcmode.soft.attached: The soft PLC is driving the gates of the live run.
plcmode.soft.ended: The live run ended, so the soft PLC stopped.
plcmode.res.unbound: Tags the program does not declare
plcmode.needLive: Start Live in Run first: a PLC talks to the model while it runs at the pace of the clock.
plcmode.needAck: Tick the box first: simulation only, and you are responsible.
plcmode.real.intro: The model plays the plant, a real PLC plays the controller. Each cycle the model's sensors are written to the PLC's coils and registers and the PLC's output coils are read back to the gates. Studio opens the connection; the PLC must be on this computer or a private network.
plcmode.real.browser: Real mode needs CadCraft Studio: a browser tab cannot open a raw TCP connection. Soft mode works fully here.
plcmode.real.oldStudio: This CadCraft Studio has no PLC client yet; it needs the 0.9 build. Soft mode works here.
plcmode.hostNote: The address and port stay on this computer. They are not saved in the model file, and there is no password: Modbus TCP has none.
plcmode.problem.unknown_tag: {tag}: the layout has no such tag.
plcmode.problem.wrong_table: {tag}: Studio writes coils and holding registers only.
plcmode.problem.bad_type: {tag}: a coil or discrete input holds a bit.
plcmode.problem.overlap: {tag}: another tag is on the same address.
plcmode.problem.bad_scale: {tag}: the scale must not be zero.
plcmode.ack: I understand: simulation only, never unattended, and I am responsible for what the PLC does.
plcmode.real.connect.hint: Needs a live run, a clean map and the box ticked
plcmode.real.on: Connected to {host}:{port}. The gates follow the PLC.
plcmode.real.ended: The live run ended, so the PLC link was closed.
plcmode.real.lost: The PLC link was lost ({why}). The gates are closed.
plcmode.note: A PLC cannot make a belt run faster: loads move kinematically. This is not a safety validation.
problem.orders-missing: {id} is set to take orders from a file, but no orders table is chosen. Open an orders file in the Orders section and pick it here.
problem.orders-empty: {id} is set to take orders from a file, but the table has no rows for it (a row with no source column goes to every such source).
orders.title: Orders from a file
orders.note: Arrivals from a CSV file instead of random times: set a source to Orders from a file and pick the table. The first row names the columns: time_s, time_min, time_h or time (when it arrives, counted from the start of the run), or clock (h:mm:ss, counted from the first row); type, length_m or length_mm, qty, source (a source's id) and order (a label). Only the time column is needed. The same file gives the same run. If a row cannot be read, nothing is loaded and the first bad row is shown.
orders.name: Table name
orders.summary: {rows} rows, {count} loads, first at {first}, last at {last} (file {file}).
orders.unit: A column named just time is in
orders.noSample: The sample orders file could not be loaded.
orders.tooMany: Ten orders tables are the most; remove one first.
orders.err.no-time-column: There is no time column. Name one of time_s, time_min, time_h, time or clock in the first row.
orders.err.bad-header: The time unit is not one this file can use.
orders.err.bad-time: Line {line}, column {column}: '{value}' is not a number.
orders.err.negative-time: Line {line}, column {column}: '{value}' is before the start of the run.
orders.err.bad-clock: Line {line}, column {column}: '{value}' is not a time of day (h:mm or h:mm:ss).
orders.err.bad-type: Line {line}, column {column}: '{value}' is not a type name (letters, digits, _ and - only, up to 40).
orders.err.bad-length: Line {line}, column {column}: '{value}' is not a length above 0 and up to 20 m.
orders.err.bad-qty: Line {line}, column {column}: '{value}' is not a whole number from 1 to 1000.
orders.err.bad-source: Line {line}, column {column}: '{value}' is not a source id.
orders.err.short-row: Line {line}: the row has no value in the time column.
orders.err.too-many-cells: Line {line}: the row has more values than the first row has columns.
orders.err.too-many-rows: Line {line}: more than 50,000 rows; split the file.
orders.err.bad-quote: Line {line}: a quote is opened and never closed.
